source.title: Learning In-context n-grams with Transformers: Sub-n-grams Are Near-stationary Points
source.authors: A. Varre; Gizem Yüce; Nicolas Flammarion

record.tranche_reason: The paper gives theoretical and experimental results on sub-n-gram solutions and staged training, refining the single-transition account. Its experiments use a different synthetic n-gram setup and measures from the original induction-head study.
record.gate_note: The paper directly constructs sub-n-gram estimators in an attention-only transformer and reports their gradient behavior, attention patterns during training, and loss-curve stages. It does not report cited findings from other work as its own results. It does not measure loss falling with token index or a training-loss bump, and it does not test few-shot task learning.
record.test_reason: The paper's own toy experiments and theory bear on how induction-like circuits form. Small attention-only transformers on in-context trigrams move through plateaus: uniform, then previous-token (bigram), then attention to the (−2)-token (trigram). Loss jumps coincide with these attention shifts. Theory shows sub-n-gram configurations are near-stationary points, which explains the plateaus. This argues formation is several transitions (V7) and qualifies the single phase change (V2).
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that k-gram estimators (k<n) built in a simplified two-layer transformer are near-stationary points of the population cross-entropy loss. This explains why training lingers on plateaus at sub-n-gram solutions before escaping to learn longer histories. Their toy experiments show discrete transitions between these solutions.
record.recipe_differences: Rather than reproducing the original induction-head measurement, the paper analyzes constructed sub-n-gram estimators and trains small transformers on synthetic in-context n-gram prediction tasks. It adds a near-stationary-point analysis and reports staged attention and loss behavior.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported training dynamics differ by architecture: the attention-only experiments show successive relative-token stages, while the MLP-layer experiment has one intermediate plateau and a head attending to both (−1, −2)-tokens. One-hot and learned embeddings are both tested; the paper also reports the relative-token ordering across five seeds.
record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning, Proceedings of Machine Learning Research 267 (2025)
record.problems: The theory is asymptotic in sequence length and parameter scale. Experiments use small synthetic n-gram tasks and limited model configurations; many outcomes are qualitative descriptions of plots rather than tabulated values. No control experiments or uncertainty estimates are reported. The paper itself notes limitations involving finite sequence lengths and practical training conditions.

untested.parts: Second-layer attention (history matching and copying) in trained models; causal composition with the previous-token head; real-text [A][B]…[A] prompts.
Loss falling with token index; a training-loss bump; whether the transition window is early in training in realistic models.
Entirely untested (no large models, no share of ICL).
Real model families, larger sizes, other modalities; seed variation beyond five toy runs.
No systematic variation of data or training setup.
Overlap of transitions and settings beyond synthetic n-gram tasks.

record.verdict_notes: Peer-reviewed at ICML 2025. The setting is Edelman-style in-context Markov/n-gram data, and the circuit is a statistical induction head. Evidence is mostly qualitative plots with no uncertainty. The theory is asymptotic in sequence length and parameter scale. r3's value conflicts with the Figure 3 caption (uniform attention at the first checkpoint). The Figure 4 step labels exceed the stated 4096 iterations.

versions.untested_parts: Tests constructed history-matching and copy behavior in simplified n-gram transformers, with attention patterns in small trained models. It does not causally intervene on the proposed circuit or test the classic [A][B] … [A] prompt pattern separately.

Tests staged training and attention changes on synthetic n-gram tasks. It does not measure loss falling with token index, a bump in the training loss, or whether such a bump coincides with the same induction-head formation event.
Does not test large transformers or whether induction heads account for most in-context learning.

Tests a simplified transformer, attention-only transformer variants, and an MLP-layer variant, with limited seed experiments. It does not test broad model families, large model sizes, other modalities, or universality across training runs generally.
Does not systematically vary training-data properties or training setup to test their effect on induction-head formation or persistence of in-context learning.
Does not test few-shot task learning or compare its mechanisms with induction heads.
Reports several stages in particular synthetic n-gram training setups; it does not establish how many distinct transitions occur generally or whether transitions overlap in other settings.

rows.subject: simplified disentangled transformer, parameter configuration θ*k
rows.size_stated: Vocabulary S; embedding dimension d, with d ≥ S
rows.operation_detail: Constructed parameters intended to implement a k-gram estimator
rows.measure: Next-token prediction implements the k-gram maximum-likelihood estimator by matching histories and averaging following tokens
rows.value: The construction implements the k-gram estimator in the limit c → ∞
rows.note: The first-layer heads retrieve relative-position tokens; the second layer matches histories and aggregates the tokens that follow matching histories. This is a constructed solution, not evidence that the circuit forms spontaneously in general models.
rows.check: A hand-built parameter configuration, not a trained model. It shows the two-layer history-matching circuit can implement the k-gram estimator, not that it forms in training.

rows.subject: simplified disentangled transformer, parameter configuration θ*k
rows.size_stated: Vocabulary S; embedding dimension d, with d ≥ S
rows.operation_detail: Bounded the population-loss gradient at constructed k-gram parameters
rows.measure: Norm of the population cross-entropy gradient
rows.value: The gradient vanishes in the stated infinite sequence-length and parameter-scale limit; the configurations are called near-stationary points
rows.note: This supports the proposed stationary sub-n-gram solutions, but does not itself measure a training trajectory moving between them.
rows.check: Theoretical (asymptotic, T,c→∞) near-stationarity result, not a measurement. It supports plateaus at sub-n-gram solutions as an argument only.

source_check.correct: Theorem: the population-loss gradient vanishes along c = Θ(T) → ∞ at constructed k-gram parameters. This is a theoretical result, not a measurement of formation dynamics; state cannot_determine for V7 by itself.
source_check.locator_found: Section 4.2, Theorem 4.1 and the paragraph immediately following it.
source_check.problem: A stationary-point construction is recorded as an observed training trajectory.

rows.operation_detail: Inspected first-layer attention patterns during training
rows.measure: Tokens attended to by the first-layer heads
rows.value: Both heads focus on the previous token, the (−1)-token
rows.note: The authors describe this as the model behaving like a bigram estimator at the first plateau.
rows.check: Value likely wrong. Figure 3 caption says heads first attend uniformly; previous-token attention comes at the second plateau. The t=115 checkpoint is the uniform stage. It bears on V7 as the initial stage, not on V1.

source_check.correct: At the initial t = 115 checkpoint, both heads attend uniformly to previous positions. Previous-token attention belongs to the later t = 5000 checkpoint. The initial snapshot alone cannot establish V7.
source_check.locator_found: Figure 3 checkpoint labels and caption; Section 5 discussion.
source_check.problem: The row assigns the later previous-token pattern to the initial uniform-attention checkpoint; the discussion's plateau numbering is inconsistent with the caption.

rows.subject: simplified disentangled transformer
rows.value: Learning occurs in distinct phases, with extended plateaus followed by quick jumps to the next phase
rows.note: The text describes the pattern qualitatively; no numerical loss values are stated. This is test loss, not the claimed token-index loss or a reported training-loss bump.
rows.check: For V2: abrupt jumps after plateaus are observed, but there are several, and this is test loss with no token-index ICL measure or bump. For V7 the state is observed.

source_check.correct: V7: observed staged learning with prolonged plateaus and quick transitions. V2: partial evidence concerning abrupt transitions; no token-index ICL measure or coincident loss bump is reported.
source_check.locator_found: Section 5 experimental setup and discussion; Figure 3a.
source_check.problem: A single partial state understates the observed V7 trajectory and conflates it with the incomplete V2 measurement.

rows.subject: attention-only transformer with one-hot embeddings
rows.size_stated: Vocabulary S = 3; embedding dimension d = S + T; sequence length T = 32
rows.stage_stated: training steps shown at t = 115, 5000, and 16000
rows.operation_detail: Inspected first-layer attention patterns during training

conditions.value: Adam, weight decay 0.0001, learning rate 0.005, batch size 128; 4096 iterations

rows.value: Initially both heads attend uniformly; at a later plateau both attend to the previous token, and by the end the second head attends to the (−2)-token
rows.note: The described progression is across the plotted checkpoints; the paper also reports that at the second plateau one head may not yet be formed while the other attends to the previous token.
rows.check: Checkpoints t=115/5000/16000 are captioned in Figure 4, yet training is stated as 4096 iterations. The step labels may be copied from Figure 3. First-layer attention only.

source_check.correct: Figure 4 describes uniform attention initially; at the second plateau either both heads attend to the previous token or only one has formed; the second head subsequently attends to the (−2)-token. Appendix I.1 states 4096 iterations despite Figure 4 labels t = 5000 and 16000. V7 progression is observed; V1 composition and V4 induction-head behaviour are not directly established.
source_check.problem: The value omits the caption's alternative plateau pattern; checkpoint labels conflict with the stated training duration, and version states exceed the first-layer evidence.

rows.subject: attention-only transformers, five random seeds
rows.operation_detail: Compared attention patterns across random seeds
rows.measure: Which relative-position token is attended to first
rows.value: Across the five seeds, the transformers attend to the (−1)-token first rather than the (−2)-token; the paper says they never attend to (−2) before attending to (−1)
rows.note: The paper reports this as an aggregate statement across five seeds; attention maps are shown separately in the figure.
rows.check: Five seeds, shown qualitatively. The (−1)-token is attended before the (−2)-token in every seed.

source_check.correct: Figure 5 reports (−1)-token attention preceding (−2)-token attention across five seeds, repeating the Figure 3 procedure. This supports ordering of V7 sub-steps; it does not directly identify induction behaviour across runs for V4.
source_check.problem: The five-seed result concerns first-layer positional attention, not verified induction-head behaviour.

rows.subject: 4-gram language-model training experiment
rows.size_stated: 4-gram task; other model details not stated at the figure
rows.operation_detail: Compared test-loss trajectory with losses of sub-n-gram estimators
rows.measure: Test loss and unigram, bigram, trigram, and 4-gram estimator losses
rows.note: The accompanying text says training phases overlap with the sub-n-gram estimator losses; the figure supplies no tabulated values.
rows.check: Figure only (4-gram). Plateaus align with unigram, bigram and trigram estimator losses. No attention data for this run.

rows.subject: simplified transformer
rows.size_stated: Vocabulary S = 5; sequence length L = 128; 3-gram language model
rows.value: Gradient norm stays low during plateau stages and spikes during jumps between plateaus
rows.note: Qualitative result; no numeric gradient values are stated.

rows.subject: transformer with MLP layers
rows.size_stated: Vocabulary S = 5; sequence length L = 64; two-layer setup
rows.operation_detail: Inspected attention behavior and gradient norms during training
rows.measure: Intermediate plateaus, attention behavior, and gradient norm
rows.baseline: attention-only transformer comparison described in text
rows.value: There is a single intermediate plateau, unlike the attention-only transformers; one head attends to both the (−1, −2)-tokens after the plateau. Gradient norm is low at plateaus and spikes during jumps
rows.note: The paper says the plateau corresponds to the unigram. The attention pattern and number of plateaus differ from the attention-only setup.
rows.check: With MLP layers there is only one intermediate plateau (unigram). One head attends to both (−1) and (−2) at once, so the sub-steps merge. Induction-head status is unclear because the second layer is not shown.

source_check.correct: V7: partial, with one intermediate unigram plateau and a head acquiring (−1, −2)-token attention together afterward. V4: cannot_determine, because induction behaviour of the second-layer head is not measured.
source_check.problem: Partial fits the architectural qualification of V7, but untested V4 behaviour requires cannot_determine.

statements.correction: Metric: cross-entropy test loss. Theorem 4.1: gradient vanishes along c = Θ(T) → ∞. Checkpoints t = 5000 and t = 16000 refer consistently to the simplified model in Figure 3.
statements.problem: The study reports cross-entropy test loss, not a stated KL metric. The asymptotic gradient result also needs the coordinated scaling specified by the theorem.
